Flag temporally inconsistent iSNVs in longitudinal data

Source: R/qc-temporal.R
flagTemporalInconsistency.Rd

For longitudinal samples from the same host, identifies iSNVs that appear at only one timepoint (transient) versus those detected at multiple consecutive timepoints (persistent). Transient iSNVs are more likely to be sequencing artefacts; persistent ones are more likely genuine within-host variants.

Usage

flagTemporalInconsistency(
  whe,
  hostCol = "host_id",
  timeCol = "timepoint",
  minTimepoints = 2L,
  minConsecutive = NULL,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with longitudinal samples from the same host.

hostCol

Character scalar. Column name in colData for host identifier (default: "host_id").

timeCol

Character scalar. Column name in colData for time point (default: "timepoint"). It must hold numbers, dates, date-times, time differences or a factor whose levels are in time order; text is read as numbers when every value is one, and is otherwise an error, since text such as "day10" and "day2" has no time order. A blank or NA is a missing timepoint.

minTimepoints

Integer scalar. Minimum number of distinct timepoints at which an iSNV must be detected to be considered persistent (default: 2). Replicate samples taken at one timepoint count as one timepoint.

minConsecutive

Integer scalar. Minimum number of consecutive timepoints required, counted over the distinct timepoints at which the host was sampled. If NULL (default), any minTimepoints detections suffice regardless of consecutiveness. Set to 2 or 3 for stricter filtering.

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), only consider QC-passed entries; a cell whose qcPass is NA counts as not passed.

Value

A WithinHostExperiment with updated qcPass assay and a new column temporal_class in mcols(rowRanges). Sites are classified within each host; a transient site is flagged only in the samples of the hosts where it is transient. The site-level temporal_class is "persistent" if the site is persistent in at least one host, "transient" if it is transient in every host where it was detected, and NA where it was never detected.

Details

This check applies only where a host was sampled at more than one timepoint. Detections are counted per distinct timepoint: a site called in any sample taken at a timepoint, including any of its technical replicates, is detected at that timepoint, so replicates alone cannot make a site persistent. A host sampled at a single timepoint, however many replicates it has, is not classified. Samples whose timepoint is NA are not counted, with a warning, but are flagged with the rest of their host. Transient sites are flagged by setting qcPass to FALSE where it was TRUE; NA cells are left as they are.

The biological rationale: genuine within-host variants arise from viral replication and should persist (or change smoothly) across consecutive timepoints. An iSNV that appears once at 5% and is absent at all other timepoints is more likely a sequencing or library preparation artefact.

The function records the filtering step in qcLog with step name "temporal_consistency".

References

Farjo M et al. (2024). Within-host evolutionary dynamics and tissue compartmentalization during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. J. Virol. 98:e01618-23. doi:10.1128/jvi.01618-23

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200, 300), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "C", "G")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("T", "G", "A")
freq <- matrix(c(0.1, NA,  0.2,   # var1: 2 timepoints
                 0.05, NA,  NA,    # var2: 1 timepoint (transient)
                 0.15, 0.2, 0.1),  # var3: 3 timepoints
               nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = freq),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("t1", "t2", "t3"),
        host_id = c("H1", "H1", "H1"),
        timepoint = c(1, 2, 3)))
whe <- flagTemporalInconsistency(whe, minTimepoints = 2L)
S4Vectors::mcols(SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(whe))$temporal_class
#> [1] "persistent" "transient"  "persistent"
